acting a little too boisterous on the plane, on the boat, and during lunch, ...because Rosa had cautioned her several times.

contexts.UP:

contexts.note: Both because clauses attach Rosa’s warnings as the reason for boisterousness, instead of warnings resulting from it.

findings.sourceReading: Maria was too noisy on the plane, boat, and at lunch, and repeatedly received warnings from Rosa as a result.
findings.alternative: A reader can infer the ordinary reason for warnings from context, but the English explicitly makes warnings the cause of the noise rather than its response.

findings.sourceReading: The adults realize they naturally would not want their children present for the sordid inheritance discussion.
findings.alternative: The intended meaning is fully recoverable, but ‘they’d wouldn’t’ is not a valid English auxiliary sequence.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: UP’s ‘slightly emotionally’ is an unidiomatic rendering of Rosa becoming somewhat emotional as she shouts at the children.

contexts.MG:
Rosa yelled at the children, slightly overcome with emotion.
The children didn't understand why they were suddenly being yelled at this time, but Eva and the rest realized it too late.
They were talking so bluntly about the filthy topic of the inheritance right in front of the children.
...Of course they'd wouldn't want their children to remain.
So they all immediately agreed with Rosa's plan.
contexts.UP:
Rosa yelled at the children, slightly emotionally.
The children didn't understand why they were suddenly being yelled at now, but Eva and the rest came to the same realization as Rosa after a delay.
They were talking so grandly about the filthy topic of the inheritance in front of the children.
...There was no way that they'd want their children to remain here.
So they all immediately agreed with Rosa's plan.

findings.sourceReading: Rosa is a little overcome by emotion when she orders the children back to the guesthouse.
findings.alternative: The nearby verb ‘yelled’ conveys her agitation, but the adverbial phrase itself is not idiomatic English.
